newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. arms inspector to visit Baghdad on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: U.N. arms inspector to visit Baghdad on Saturday.

text.p: U.N. senior arms inspector Rolf Ekeus will on Saturday arrive in Baghdad for discussions on his report that Iraq might be hiding quantities of banned arms, a U.N. source said.
The Baghdad source on Thursday said Ekeus will stay until Monday and will be accompanied by other U.N. arms experts.
The source, from the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of ridding Iraq of weapons of mass-destruction added:" He will hold discussions with the Iraqi side."
In a major half-year report he submitted to the U.N. Security Council on October 11, Ekeus said Iraq might still be hiding small but significant quantities of banned arms.
"I am sure the discussions (with Iraqi officials) will also centre on that report," the source said.
Ridding Iraq of nuclear, chemical and biological weapons is a key requirement for lifting stringent trade sanctions imposed after Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.

Ekeus' deputy Charles Duelfer was in Baghdad this month. Iraq gave him nine letters attempting to clarify its disclosure of banned weapons after the U.N. official told the press that Baghdad's original declarations were flawed and incomplete.
